questions.q: The heart has how many chambers?
questions.exp: Four chambers: right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle.
optExp: Includes coronary sinus, but standard answer is 4.

questions.q: The left ventricle pumps blood into the:
questions.exp: LV → aorta → systemic circulation. RV → pulmonary trunk → lungs.

questions.q: The right atrium receives blood from:
opts: The superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, and coronary sinus
questions.exp: RA receives deoxygenated blood from SVC, IVC, and coronary sinus.

questions.q: The bicuspid (mitral) valve is between:
opts: The right atrium and right ventricle
The right ventricle and pulmonary artery
The left atrium and left ventricle
The superior vena cava and right atrium
questions.exp: Mitral (bicuspid) valve sits between LA and LV. Tricuspid is right-sided. SL valves at outflows.

questions.q: The first branch of the aorta is the:
questions.exp: The first branches of the aorta are the coronary arteries (from the aortic sinuses). Brachiocephalic is the first arch branch.
optExp: First arch branch, but coronaries arise even earlier from the root.

questions.q: The left coronary artery (LCA) divides into:
opts: The posterior descending artery and right marginal artery
The left anterior descending artery and circumflex artery
The right coronary artery and circumflex artery
The left anterior descending artery and diagonal branches
The marginal artery and posterior descending artery
questions.exp: LCA divides into the LAD (left anterior descending) and circumflex artery, supplying most of the left ventricle.

questions.q: In ~80% of people, the posterior descending artery (PDA) arises from the:
opts: From the left anterior descending artery
From the left main coronary artery
questions.exp: ~80% of people are right-coronary dominant — PDA arises from RCA, supplying inferior LV and posterior septum.
optExp: PDA never arises from aorta directly.

questions.q: The SA node is located in the:
opts: The right atrium at the entrance of the superior vena cava
questions.exp: SA node sits in the right atrial wall near the superior vena cava entry — the heart's natural pacemaker.
optExp: LA is not the pacemaker location.
AV node is in the AV groove.

questions.q: The AV node delays conduction to allow:
opts: Allow adequate ventricular filling before contraction
Increase the heart rate during exercise
Stimulate the SA node to fire
questions.exp: AV nodal delay (~100 ms) allows the atria to fully empty into the ventricles before ventricular contraction.

questions.q: The vagus nerve (CN X) provides parasympathetic innervation to the heart, primarily slowing the:
questions.exp: Vagal stimulation slows SA node firing (also slows AV conduction). Has minimal effect on ventricular contractility.
optExp: Vagal effect on ventricular force is minimal.
AV node is also affected, but SA is primary.
Baroreceptors send signals TO vagus, not from.

questions.q: Cardiac veins drain into the:
questions.exp: Most cardiac venous blood drains into the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium.

questions.q: The thoracic duct drains into the:
questions.exp: The thoracic duct (largest lymphatic vessel) drains most of the body's lymph into the left venous angle (junction of left subclavian and internal jugular).
optExp: IVC is venous, not lymph drainage.
Portal vein is for GI venous return.

questions.q: The right lymphatic duct drains lymph from the:
opts: Lower body and left upper body
Right head, neck, and right arm
Entire body except right upper quadrant
questions.exp: The right lymphatic duct drains the right upper quadrant; thoracic duct drains the rest.

questions.q: Primary lymphoid organs include:
questions.exp: Primary lymphoid organs (where lymphocytes mature) = bone marrow (B cells) and thymus (T cells). Secondary = spleen, LNs, MALT.
optExp: Spleen and lymph nodes are secondary lymphoid organs.

questions.q: Lymph nodes function to:
questions.exp: Lymph nodes filter antigens from lymph and present them to lymphocytes, initiating adaptive responses.

questions.q: The spleen is located in which abdominal quadrant?
questions.exp: The spleen sits in the left upper quadrant, posterior to ribs 9-11, lateral to the stomach.

questions.q: The spleen's white pulp contains:
questions.exp: White pulp contains periarteriolar lymphoid sheaths (PALS, T cells) and B cell follicles. Red pulp filters blood and stores platelets.

questions.q: The cisterna chyli is found at the level of:
questions.exp: Cisterna chyli is a saccular dilation at the start of the thoracic duct at L1-L2, receiving lumbar and intestinal trunks.
optExp: Diaphragmatic hiatus is at T12 — close but L1-L2 is the standard answer.

questions.q: Lymphoedema can result from:
questions.exp: Obstruction or removal of lymphatic vessels (e.g. mastectomy with axillary clearance, filariasis) causes lymph accumulation.
optExp: Hyperthyroidism causes pretibial myxoedema in Graves, but different.

questions.q: The thymus is most active in:
questions.exp: Thymus is most active in early life, producing mature T cells. It involutes (shrinks) after puberty.

questions.q: The apex of the heart is normally located at:
opts: 2nd intercostal space at the right midclavicular line
5th intercostal space at the left midclavicular line
At the level of the xiphoid process
6th intercostal space at the right midclavicular line
questions.exp: The cardiac apex (LV) is normally palpated at the 5th left intercostal space in the midclavicular line.
optExp: This is the area for aortic auscultation.

questions.q: Stenosis of which valve typically causes a crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur radiating to the carotids?
questions.exp: Aortic stenosis produces an ejection systolic murmur, loudest at the right 2nd intercostal space, radiating to carotids.
optExp: Pulmonary stenosis murmur in left 2nd ICS.

questions.q: Axillary lymph nodes drain the:
questions.exp: Axillary nodes drain the upper extremity, lateral breast, and thoracoabdominal wall — important in breast cancer staging.
optExp: Pelvis drains via internal iliac nodes.
Lower limb drains to inguinal nodes.

questions.q: S1 heart sound is produced by:
opts: Atrioventricular valve closure at ventricular systole
questions.exp: S1 ('lub') = closure of mitral and tricuspid valves at the start of systole. S2 ('dub') = SL closure.

questions.q: S2 heart sound is produced by:
opts: Aortic and pulmonary valve closure at ventricular diastole
questions.exp: S2 = closure of aortic and pulmonary valves, marking end of systole.

questions.q: The pericardium consists of:
questions.exp: Pericardium = tough outer fibrous + inner serous (parietal lines fibrous; visceral = epicardium on heart). Pericardial fluid in between.
optExp: Endocardium is the heart's inner lining.
